text:
zoe: Customer AcmeApp reports their JSON mode streaming responses are intermittently cut off. Parser error: 'Unexpected EOF while parsing object' on their side. Seen on production hosted API only.

acme_integration: Confirmed — ~0.3% of streams we see end in an unclosed object. Happening across multiple endpoints (chat + structured JSON). We capture the raw stream and it stops mid-object.

jon: Can you paste a minimal raw snippet?

acme_integration: here's an anonymized tail from their connection (we truncated headers):
```
data: {"id":"msg_abc","type":"response","payload":{"result":{"name":"Alice","age":30},
data: {"id":"msg_abc","type":"response","payload":{"result":{"name":"Bob","age":25},
```
The stream ends right after the second object but missing closing braces.

liam: Any pattern on connection path? edge region, proxy hop, or specific LB?

acme_integration: Most traces show CloudFront -> our edge -> api-gw -> runtime. Some show an extra corporate proxy in customer path.

maya: Repro attempt from our side with curl: 
```
curl -v -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"mode":"json","prompt":"..."}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/chat
```
From our sandbox sometimes we get a clean stream, sometimes it ends with an incomplete JSON chunk.

eng-runtime: Putting on the runtime queue. Two lines of investigation: 1) are we flushing a half-chunk due to keepalive/window? 2) any premature connection FIN from upstream or the edge idle timeout.

zoe: Support-bot created INC#12345 and attached the customer's raw capture + correlation IDs. @eng-runtime do you want the pcap or just the server side traces?

support-bot: Incident INC-12345 created by zoe. Links: <https://incidents.redwood/INC-12345|INC-12345>.

eng-runtime: Please attach both. Also include the stream sequence numbers and X-Request-ID. We'll search for 'last-chunk' markers.

liam: Quick note — we saw similar behavior before with proxy TLS renegotiation leading to a short FIN. That produced mid-frame EOFs where the SSE payload ended in the middle of a JSON object. Could be a client side keepalive mismatch.

acme_integration: Customer provided curl --max-time 60 and said it happened on average 1 in 300 requests. They run an intermittent corporate proxy that injects keepalive probes.

jon: Can we add a defensive server-side behavior: on SSE streams if we detect a trailing partial JSON on disconnect, append a minimal sentinel event or add a 'stream_error' terminal event with parseable JSON explaining it was truncated? That would help clients not crash.

eng-runtime: Good idea. Two concerns: changing streaming protocol semantics might break callers expecting strict JSON per event. But we can emit an explicit final control event like `event: redwood-terminated` with JSON payload describing reason. Backwards compatible when clients ignore unknown events.

maya: For immediate mitigation, recommend customer-level workaround: implement a streaming stitcher that buffers until it sees a complete JSON object and retries on reconnect using the last token position. We can also offer them a dedicated retry header to request a final summary event.

zoe: I'll propose the 'redwood-terminated' event as an interim fix and collect more traces. @eng-runtime please post ETA for a patch.

eng-runtime: ETA for a soft-fail header/event: 3 business days for a patch to the hosted runtime, then rollout to canary. Also we'll add additional metrics to track partial-closure rate by edge region.

liam: Also add an alert if >0.05% truncated-streams in a minute window.

acme_integration: Thanks — we'll pass the mitigation notes to the customer. They've agreed to try the buffer-and-stitch approach while you patch.

zoe: Follow-ups: attach pcap + X-Request-IDs to INC-12345, eng-runtime to post PR with event schema, and support to notify customer post-canary. :thumbsup:

support-bot: INC-12345 updated: pcap and traces uploaded.

eng-runtime: Uploaded diff for review: adds `event: redwood-terminated` with payload {"reason":"truncated_stream","correlation_id":"<id>"} and a runtime flag to enable on canary.

zoe: Great, thanks. We'll keep this thread updated with customer feedback.
